text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Ho Chi Minh City plans to move 500,000 people from the inner city to planned new areas on the outskirts.
-- Agreements have been signed with Thailand and Canada to examine the coal and tourism industries in northeast Quang Ninh province and pollution in Halong Bay.
-- Cabinet ministers have discussed and passed a draft amendment to rules governing implementation of the domestic investment law.
-- A German bank has sent copies of three counterfeit guarantees from the State Bank of Vietnam which are currently in circulation on the international financial market.

-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has told Cambodia's First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh he hopes remaining problems between the two countries can be solved soon based on mutual respect of the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
-- Vietnam's consummer prices rose by 1.8 percent in February from levels in January.
-- One person has been killed and two injured in a boat collision in the central coastal province of Binh Dinh.
-- Vietnam sold 50 billion dong ($4.46 million) worth of one-year treasury notes with an annual coupon of 11.50 percent to three domestic banks in an auction on Wednesday.
-- The government has issued new rules on fines for administrative violations in the banking system.
-- Industrial output growth for February is expected to reach 13.9 percent.
-- Vietnam's government held a monthly meeting to discuss measures to overcome budget revenue problems and the trade deficit.
